questions.stem: What is the main purpose of CLZ-140's resource group?

options.A: A replacement for an Azure tenant.
options.C: An understandable lifecycle boundary for the lesson.
options.D: A Terraform provider installer.

optionExplanations.A: Identity directories are separate.
optionExplanations.B: A group does not provide compute.
optionExplanations.C: Related managed objects can share ownership and cleanup context.
optionExplanations.D: Initialization installs providers locally.

questions.stem: With name_prefix=campus and environment=dev, which group name follows CLZ-140's expression?

options.D: campus-dev-clz140-rg

optionExplanations.A: That changes the input and ordering.
optionExplanations.B: That uses the wrong lesson code.
optionExplanations.C: That omits environment and lesson identity.
optionExplanations.D: The fixed lesson code is normalized to clz140.

questions.stem: Which supplied tag identifies this particular exercise's ownership context?

options.D: Project = CLZ-140

optionExplanations.A: It separates this lesson from others.
optionExplanations.B: Environment contains dev, test, or prod.
optionExplanations.C: ManagedBy contains Terraform.
optionExplanations.D: Project contains the curriculum name.

questions.stem: The tag map has Environment = var.environment. What is Environment in that expression?

options.D: The Terraform local resource address.

optionExplanations.A: The key does not select a subscription.
optionExplanations.B: The input supplies its value.
optionExplanations.C: Location is a separate property.
optionExplanations.D: A tag key is not an address.

questions.stem: A VM is added to a tagged group but has no tags in its own resource definition. What should the author know?

options.A: Every group tag is inherited automatically.
options.B: Terraform always copies parent tags implicitly.
options.C: Resource-group tags do not automatically flow to contained resources.
options.D: The VM inherits only the Lab tag.

optionExplanations.A: Azure does not provide automatic tag inheritance.
optionExplanations.B: Resource arguments must express that behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Apply tags explicitly or use an approved policy.
optionExplanations.D: No built-in selective inheritance occurs.

questions.stem: Can one resource group contain resources deployed in different Azure regions?

options.A: No; every object must use the group's region.
options.B: Only if the group has no tags.
options.C: Only if all resources are Windows.
options.D: Yes; group location stores group metadata.

optionExplanations.A: A group is not a single-region placement requirement.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not govern this capability.
optionExplanations.C: Operating system is unrelated.
optionExplanations.D: Contained resources have their own location choices.

questions.stem: The learner adds an Owner entry to local.tags. What should the next plan be inspected for?

options.A: The intended tag update and any unexpected changes.
options.D: An automatic VM deployment.

optionExplanations.A: The exercise asks for a reviewed metadata change.
optionExplanations.B: Adding a tag does not change tenant.
optionExplanations.C: A tag expression does not erase state.
optionExplanations.D: No VM resource is declared.

questions.stem: Why cannot the learner select lab_id through the documented inputs?

options.A: Azure forbids all custom tag values.
options.B: The lesson fixes lab_id in locals.
options.C: The site hides a fifth required input.
options.D: The identity is generated from current time.

optionExplanations.A: Azure supports custom values.
optionExplanations.B: It is not part of the variable interface.
optionExplanations.C: The source declares four public inputs.
optionExplanations.D: The provided local uses a fixed literal.

questions.stem: Which command reads CLZ-140's group name and tags from Azure?

options.D: az account get-access-token

optionExplanations.A: Formatting does not query Azure.
optionExplanations.B: Provider listing does not show actual group tags.
optionExplanations.C: The query returns the deployed group's properties.
optionExplanations.D: Token acquisition is not metadata readback.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: What does a CostCenter tag added in a production version do by itself?

options.C: Cap all Azure charges at zero.
options.D: Classify resources for governance and reporting.

optionExplanations.A: A tag is not a payment action.
optionExplanations.B: RBAC controls access.
optionExplanations.C: Budgets and cost controls are separate.
optionExplanations.D: It supplies metadata; separate processes use it.

questions.stem: Which proposed tag value is unsuitable for resource metadata?

options.D: The environment label dev.

optionExplanations.A: Tags are not a secret store.
optionExplanations.B: That is ordinary classification metadata.
optionExplanations.C: That supports lifecycle tracking.
optionExplanations.D: That is already part of the standard map.

questions.stem: After apply, the group lacks an expected tag. What should be investigated?

options.B: The local map and applicable Azure Policy behavior.
options.C: Whether the inspected object is the intended group.
options.D: Only the local dependency lock-file timestamp.

optionExplanations.A: No VM is deployed.
optionExplanations.B: Configuration or policy can affect metadata.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong object or context can produce misleading tag readback.
optionExplanations.D: Dependency timestamps do not establish the applied tag map or policy effects.

questions.stem: A manually created unrelated disk appears in the lab group. Why review ownership before destroy?

options.C: Deleting the group can remove contained resources.
options.D: A Lab tag guarantees the disk's ownership.

optionExplanations.A: It can delete contained objects.
optionExplanations.B: Being outside Terraform state is not protection from group deletion.
optionExplanations.C: The lifecycle boundary must remain disposable and owned.
optionExplanations.D: Group metadata cannot prove every object's ownership.

questions.stem: Which value marks the intended management tooling in CLZ-140?

options.D: ManagedBy = Terraform

optionExplanations.A: Windows is not the supplied tooling value.
optionExplanations.B: That is the wrong key purpose.
optionExplanations.C: That swaps identities rather than identifies tooling.
optionExplanations.D: It records the management source.

questions.stem: A tag query unexpectedly finds nothing. Which basic context check is appropriate?

options.A: Confirm subscription selection and exact tag values.
options.D: Replace all tag keys with wildcard credentials.

optionExplanations.A: Queries run against the selected Azure scope.
optionExplanations.B: An empty filter result is not deletion proof.
optionExplanations.C: There is no compute resource here.
optionExplanations.D: Credentials do not belong in tags.

questions.stem: Why should disposable lab infrastructure avoid sharing its resource group with long-lived production resources?

options.A: Resource groups cannot hold both kinds.
options.D: Terraform cannot read production resources.

optionExplanations.A: Azure permits it, but it is a poor lifecycle boundary.
optionExplanations.B: A group-level deletion should not affect unrelated production objects.
optionExplanations.C: Tags have no direct charge.
optionExplanations.D: The issue is ownership and blast radius, not that blanket limit.

questions.stem: A learner changes Environment from dev to test in this source. Why might the plan do more than update a tag?

options.C: The same input also changes the derived name.
options.D: Azure tags rename every regional service.

optionExplanations.A: There is no VM in this module.
optionExplanations.B: They are separate variables.
optionExplanations.C: Both naming and tags consume environment.
optionExplanations.D: The naming expression, not tag semantics, changes the name.

questions.stem: What does Project = Azure From Zero To Hero help group across lessons?

options.A: All resources in all Azure tenants.
options.D: Resources belonging to this learning project.

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not search inaccessible scopes.
optionExplanations.B: It is a project label, not hostname.
optionExplanations.C: Dependency checksums live in the lock file.
optionExplanations.D: The common value supports cross-lesson classification.

questions.stem: Why derive standard tags once in local.tags instead of repeating their text?

options.A: To keep a single consistent expression for consumers.
options.D: To create inheritance automatically.

optionExplanations.A: Centralization reduces accidental divergence.
optionExplanations.B: Resource attributes still enter state.
optionExplanations.C: Policies still apply.
optionExplanations.D: Explicit consumer arguments remain necessary.

questions.stem: What direct resource charge does adding the standard four tags introduce?

options.C: One public IP charge per key.
options.D: A mandatory Azure Storage account.

optionExplanations.A: Tag count is not compute billing.
optionExplanations.B: The lab's group and metadata have no direct charge.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not provision IPs.
optionExplanations.D: No storage resource is created for tags.

questions.stem: Which mechanism can enforce required tags across approved Azure scopes?

options.A: A naming convention with no policy evaluation.
options.D: A resource-group display name alone.

optionExplanations.A: A naming rule alone does not enforce required metadata keys.
optionExplanations.B: Filename changes do not enforce standards.
optionExplanations.C: Policy can require or modify governance metadata.
optionExplanations.D: Naming is not tag enforcement.

questions.stem: What should the learner change if the derived group name is unexpected?

options.D: Review the prefix and environment inputs plus fixed local expressions.

optionExplanations.A: State is not the naming source interface.
optionExplanations.B: That does not fix the local expression.
optionExplanations.C: Artwork is not naming logic.
optionExplanations.D: These values construct the name.

questions.stem: Which extra production tag most directly records when a disposable resource should be reviewed for removal?

options.D: A subscription token tag.

optionExplanations.A: A documented date supports lifecycle automation/review.
optionExplanations.B: Passwords must not be metadata.
optionExplanations.C: Architecture does not express expiration.
optionExplanations.D: Tokens should not be stored in tags.

questions.stem: Can one Azure resource belong to two resource groups simultaneously?

options.B: No; it belongs to one resource group.
options.D: Only Windows VMs can do so.

optionExplanations.A: Tags are not membership.
optionExplanations.B: A resource's ARM ID includes a single group boundary.
optionExplanations.C: Environment values do not alter membership semantics.
optionExplanations.D: OS type does not create multiple group membership.

questions.stem: Why run az group exists after Terraform destruction?

options.C: To verify the named group is absent in Azure.
options.D: To initialize the provider plugin.

optionExplanations.A: Exists is a read, not recreation.
optionExplanations.B: Groups do not have such a password.
optionExplanations.C: Independent readback complements tool completion.
optionExplanations.D: That is a local init concern.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: Does Lab=CLZ-140 stop another authorized administrator from modifying the group?

options.C: Yes; every tag encrypts the group.
options.D: No; tags do not replace RBAC.

optionExplanations.A: A tag is not a resource lock.
optionExplanations.B: That value is descriptive.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not encrypt resources.
optionExplanations.D: Authorization remains separate.

questions.stem: Why should an organization document its owner and cost-center tag conventions?

options.A: Different teams need consistent interpretation and reporting.
options.B: Azure requires every tag value to be identical.
options.C: The convention automatically creates remote state.
options.D: Terraform supports only the four lab keys.

optionExplanations.A: A convention makes the metadata useful.
optionExplanations.B: Organizations choose meaningful values.
optionExplanations.C: It does not configure a backend.
optionExplanations.D: Other nonsecret keys can be used.

questions.stem: A query filtered by Lab=CLZ-140 returns one result. Does that alone prove no other lab-owned resources exist?

options.A: Yes, tag filters cannot miss resources.
options.B: No; omitted or inconsistent tags can hide resources from that filter.
options.D: Only if Terraform has one output.

optionExplanations.A: Filters match metadata, not intent.
optionExplanations.B: Inventory and state review provide complementary evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Tags can be changed.
optionExplanations.D: Output count does not establish inventory or tagging completeness.

questions.stem: Why is changing name_prefix not the correct way to relocate the group?

options.A: Prefixes always contain encrypted region data.
options.B: Azure uses the first three name letters as region.
options.D: Location is controlled by the ManagedBy tag.

optionExplanations.A: The source has no such encoding.
optionExplanations.B: Placement is not determined that way.
optionExplanations.C: Prefix influences naming, not region selection.
optionExplanations.D: That tag identifies tooling.

questions.stem: Which production extension best preserves the lab's original tagging intent?

options.A: Replace all tags with administrator secrets.
options.B: Remove Environment to mix workloads indiscriminately.
options.C: Use random undocumented keys in each team.
options.D: Add owner, cost-center, classification, and expiration conventions.

optionExplanations.A: That turns metadata into a security problem.
optionExplanations.B: It loses useful classification.
optionExplanations.C: That makes reporting inconsistent.
optionExplanations.D: These extend ownership, reporting, and lifecycle context.
